model.notes: 24 layers, hidden 768, 6-mer tokenisation, truncated at 2048 tokens (12282 bp), float32 weights, pretrained on 850 multi-species genomes. Licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial). Sequences are upper-cased and non-ACGTN characters mapped to N before tokenisation. Sanctioned embedding = mean over all non-padding positions of the final hidden layer, including <cls>, which is the recipe on the model card. Layer embeddings = the same mean excluding <cls>.

ceiling.method: empirical: best of {scaled, unscaled} x {raw, pca50, pca128} x {C=1, C=0.1} logistic regression; configuration chosen on a validation carve of the training set (validation), then refit on the full training set and scored once on test
ceiling.note: Won by scaled/pca50/C=1. Interpret model scores relative to this: at or above it, the representation adds nothing over standard supervised practice on the raw features.

extra.grouping: whole chromosomes held out, then test windows with a near-duplicate in training removed (>=0.50 containment over exact 24-mers)
extra.why_not_sequence_identity: k-mer containment at the protein track's k=5 saturates on a four-letter alphabet and merges the whole genome into one cluster; the genomic confound is locus, not homology
extra.bootstrap_unit: 1000 kb genomic blocks within the held-out chromosomes; NOT the split unit, see task docstring

extra.citation: Dalla-Torre et al., The Nucleotide Transformer: Building and Evaluating Robust Foundation Models for Human Genomics (Nature Methods 2025); benchmark revised post-review. Underlying data: ENCODE Project Consortium and ENCODE SCREEN.
extra.ceiling_interpretation: comparator, not a bound: k-mer composition is a strong but far-from-perfect method for enhancer identification, so a model above this value is doing well rather than saturating

caveats: 2 test window(s) had a near-duplicate in training (segmental duplication reaching across chromosomes) and were removed before scoring. A chromosome split does not catch these on its own.

Exceeds the empirical ceiling (0.465): the representation adds over the best cheap supervised readout of k-mer composition. On this task that is a good outcome rather than saturation, because k-mer composition cannot nearly solve enhancer identification, so the ceiling is a comparator and not an attainable maximum. `derived.headroom` is therefore negative and must not be read as headroom on DN1.
Elicitation gap -0.0040 has a paired 95% interval [-0.0233, +0.0116] spanning zero (positive in 36% of block resamples); not distinguishable from no gap on this dataset.

The 95% intervals resample megabase blocks, not chromosomes. The split leaves 7 test chromosome(s), too few to resample honestly, so the interval covers variation across loci within them and not the variance of the chromosome holdout itself; the chromosome-level gap interval, in controls.extra, is [-0.0174, +0.0122].

Class names are inferred, not documented: the source repository labels the classes 0/1/2 without saying which is which. The no-enhancer class is pinned by joining to the sibling binary task; which of the two enhancer classes is tissue-invariant is inferred from their sizes. If that is backwards the two names swap and no score changes.
